blocks.text: You can use redaction profiles as part of your SaaS Security Data at Rest Scanning Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy to hide sensitive content that triggers policy rules. When sensitive content triggers a SaaS Security Data at Rest Scanning DLP rule, the Zscaler service uses the redaction profile associated with the policy rule to replace the content you want to protect with asterisk (*) or hash (#) characters. The Zscaler service supports redaction profiles for the following file types:

blocks.item: Supported File Types for Redaction Profiles
Archive (.tar, .zip)
Comma-Separated Value (.csv)
Microsoft Excel (.xls, .xlsm, .xltm, .xlsx, .xltx)
Microsoft PowerPoint (.ppt, .pptm, .ppsm, .potm, .pptx, .ppsx, .potx)
Microsoft Word (.doc, .docm, .dotm, .docx, .dotx)
PDF (.pdf): Editable and read-only files
Plain Text (.txt)
Rich Text (.rtf)
From the navigation menu, go to Data Security > DSPM > Rights Management.
Select the Redaction tab.
Click Add Profile.
The Add Redaction Profile drawer opens.
In the Add Redaction Profile drawer, specify settings for the redaction profile:
Profile Name: Enter a name of up to 128 characters for the redaction profile.
Redaction Type: Select either the Use Asterisks to Redact or Use Hash Signs to Redact option to redact sensitive data with asterisk characters (*) or hash characters (#), respectively.
See image.
Click Save and activate the change.
Go to Data Security > DSPM > Rights Management.
Select the Redaction tab.
Locate the redaction profile in the list, then click the Edit icon.
The Edit Redaction Profile drawer opens.
In the Edit Redaction Profile drawer, specify settings for the redaction profile:
Profile Name: Enter a name of up to 128 characters for the redaction profile.
Redaction Type: Select either the Use Asterisks to Redact or Use Hash Signs to Redact option to redact sensitive data with asterisk characters (*) or hash characters (#), respectively.
See image.
Click Save and activate the change.
